title: Noise operator on a coordinate slice
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\{−1,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, and let $b\in\{−1,1\}$. For $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, write $f_b(x)=f(b,x)$, and define $f_{\mathrm{odd}}=(f_1-f_{-1})/2$ and $f_{\mathrm{even}}=(f_1+f_{-1})/2$. For every real $\rho$, the restriction of the noise operator applied to $f$ at first coordinate $b$ is the function $x\mapsto b\rho\,(T_\rho f_{\mathrm{odd}})(x)+(T_\rho f_{\mathrm{even}})(x)$, where $T_\rho$ denotes the noise operator on the $n$-dimensional sign cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube
